items.t:
Food (proteins, fats,
carbohydrates, vitamins,
minerals, water)

Excretion of
end products
(CO₂, H₂O, urea,
uric acid, creatinine)
Stage I: breakdown of polymers into monomers (digestion)
Stage III: common pathway of catabolism
Electrons: NADH → I → CoQ → III → cyt c → IV → O₂

Alanine and other
glucogenic amino acids

Oxaloacetate
(mitochondria → to the
cytosol as malate)

2 NADPH
→ synthesis of fatty acids and cholesterol,
reduction of glutathione, microsomal oxidation

Nonoxidative phase:
transketolase (TPP), transaldolase
→ fructose-6-phosphate, glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate
(return to glycolysis)

Enterocyte:
resynthesis of TAG,
phospholipids and
cholesterol esters

Short- and medium-chain
fatty acids →
portal vein

HDL
(apo A-I) — cholesterol
from tissues to the liver

Acyl-CoA (shortened by 2 C)
→ returns to the cycle

Acetyl-CoA → Krebs cycle
(in the liver — ketone bodies)

succinyl-CoA–
acetoacetate CoA transferase
(absent in the liver)

Inhibited by: cholesterol (via SREBP),
glucagon (phosphorylation), statins
Activated by: insulin

Lysosome: apo B-100 → amino acids;
cholesterol esters → free cholesterol

Liver: microsomal oxidation
+ conjugation (PAPS, UDP-glucuronic acid)

Indoxyl sulfate (indican) and other
conjugates → urine

α-Keto acid
(carbon skeleton →
energy, glucose, ketones)

GABA
(main inhibitory
neurotransmitter of the CNS)

Serotonin
(mood, sleep, intestinal
motility, vascular tone)

Fumarate
(→ malate → oxaloacetate
→ aspartate; Krebs cycle)

carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I
(key enzyme; activated by
N-acetylglutamate)

amidophosphoribosyltransferase
(key enzyme; inhibited by AMP, GMP, IMP)

Salvage pathway: hypoxanthine, guanine + PRPP
→ IMP, GMP (HGPRT); adenine → AMP (APRT)

9 reactions: glycine, glutamine,
aspartate, CO₂, 2 formyl-THF
Time after a meal (h — hours, d — days; logarithmic scale)

Origin of replication (ori)
— ORC proteins bind

Helicase — separates the strands (ATP)
SSB proteins — stabilize single-stranded DNA

Leading strand: continuous
synthesis 5'→3' (DNA pol ε)

Lagging strand: Okazaki
fragments (DNA pol α, δ)

Primer removal (RNase H, FEN1)
gap filling (DNA pol δ)

Chromosome ends: telomerase
(reverse transcriptase, RNA template)
Gene: promoter (TATA box) — exons and introns

General transcription factors (TFIID...)
+ RNA polymerase II → initiation complex

Mature mRNA → through nuclear pores
to the cytoplasm → translation

Amino acid activation (cytosol):
aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, ATP → AMP + PPᵢ

Initiation: 40S + Met-tRNAi + eIF + GTP
binds the cap and finds AUG (scanning) → 80S

Elongation (for each codon):
1) aminoacyl-tRNA to the A site (eEF1, GTP)
2) peptidyl transferase (28S rRNA — ribozyme)
3) translocation (eEF2, GTP)

Termination: UAA, UAG, UGA stop codons
release factors (eRF), GTP

Post-translational modification: folding (chaperones),
proteolysis, phosphorylation, glycosylation, hydroxylation...

Lactose ABSENT: repressor binds
the operator → RNA polymerase cannot pass
→ genes are off

Lactose PRESENT: allolactose removes the repressor
from the operator → transcription
(enhanced by cAMP–CAP when glucose is low)

Base excision repair
(BER): DNA glycosylase,
AP endonuclease, pol β

Extrinsic pathway: Fas ligand, TNF-α
→ death receptors (Fas, TNFR1)

Intrinsic (mitochondrial) pathway: DNA damage,
oxidative stress, lack of growth factors

Release of cytochrome c from mitochondria
→ apoptosome (Apaf-1)

Chromatin condensation, DNA fragmentation,
apoptotic bodies → phagocytosis (without inflammation)

Adduct with DNA guanines → TP53, KRAS
mutations (G→T transversion) → lung cancer

Initiation: carcinogen → DNA damage →
irreversible mutation (proto-oncogene, suppressor gene)

Promotion: growth-promoting factors
(hormones, phorbol esters, chronic inflammation)
→ clonal proliferation of the mutant cell

Progression: additional mutations, genomic instability,
angiogenesis, escape from immune surveillance

Invasion and metastasis: E-cadherin ↓,
matrix metalloproteinases ↑, entry into vessels

Food: heme iron (meat) and
non-heme Fe³⁺ (ascorbate → Fe²⁺)

Bone marrow: via TfR1
endocytosis → heme synthesis

Splenic macrophages: senescent erythrocytes
→ heme oxygenase → Fe is reused

Initiation (tissue factor-bearing cell):
TF + VIIa → X → Xa; Xa + Va → small amount of thrombin

Amplification (platelet surface): thrombin
activates platelets and factors V, VIII, XI

Anticoagulants: antithrombin III (+ heparin),
protein C/S (thrombomodulin), TFPI

Propagation (activated platelet surface):
IXa + VIIIa (tenase) → Xa; Xa + Va (prothrombinase)
→ thrombin “burst”

Fibrinogen → fibrin monomer → fibrin polymer
→ XIIIa (transglutaminase) — stable clot

Fibrinolysis: plasminogen → plasmin (t-PA, urokinase)
→ fibrin degradation (D-dimer)

Ribosomes (rough ER): preprocollagen α-chains
(Gly–X–Y)ₙ; signal peptide is cleaved

Hydroxylation of proline and lysine:
prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases (Fe²⁺, O₂, α-KG, ascorbate)

Triple helix from three α-chains — procollagen
(C-propeptide disulfide bonds)

Procollagen peptidases cleave the N- and
C-propeptides → tropocollagen

Lysyl oxidase (Cu²⁺): cross-links
→ collagen fibrils and fibers

Negative charges bind Na⁺ and water →
gel, resistance to compression (cartilage)

Nerve impulse → sarcolemma depolarization
→ T-tubule (DHP receptor)

Ca²⁺ release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum
(ryanodine receptor)

Ca²⁺ + troponin C → tropomyosin shifts
→ myosin-binding sites on actin are exposed

New ATP binds → myosin detaches from actin
(no ATP — rigor)
ATP hydrolysis → myosin head in the “cocked” state

Relaxation: Ca²⁺-ATPase (SERCA) returns Ca²⁺
to the reticulum (ATP is consumed)

Ratio to the upper reference limit
(fold, log)
Time after pain onset (h — hours, d — days; log scale)

H⁺,K⁺-ATPase (proton pump) moves to the apical
membrane: H⁺ — into the lumen, K⁺ — into the cell

Food: sight, smell, taste (cephalic phase);
gastric distension, peptides (gastric phase)

Acidic chyme in the duodenum
(intestinal phase)

Secretin (S cells):
HCO₃⁻-rich juice
(pancreas, bile ducts)

Cholecystokinin (I cells):
enzyme-rich juice,
gallbladder contraction

Somatostatin, GIP, secretin →
gastric secretion and motility ↓

Senescent erythrocytes → hemoglobin
(spleen, liver, bone marrow macrophages)

Heme → biliverdin (heme oxygenase; CO, Fe²⁺)
→ bilirubin (biliverdin reductase, NADPH)

Unconjugated (indirect) bilirubin
+ albumin — in blood; water-insoluble, neurotoxic

Conjugated (direct) bilirubin → bile
(MRP2, active secretion — rate-limiting step)

Jaundice appearing on day 1
is pathological

Phase I — functionalization:
microsomal oxidation (cytochrome P450)
RH + O₂ + NADPH + H⁺ → ROH + H₂O + NADP⁺

Phase II — conjugation: glucuronide, sulfate,
glutathione, acetyl, methyl, glycine

Sometimes activation: reactive intermediate
(NAPQI, epoxides) → toxicity, carcinogenesis

Water-soluble, less toxic product →
excreted in urine or bile

Alcohol dehydrogenase
(cytosol; main pathway)
NAD⁺ → NADH

MEOS — CYP2E1
(microsomes; induced by
chronic drinking)

Aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH2, mitochondria)
NAD⁺ → NADH; inhibited by disulfiram

Acetate → acetyl-CoA → Krebs cycle,
fatty acids, ketone bodies

NADH/NAD⁺ ↑: lactic acidosis, hypoglycemia,
fatty liver, hyperuricemia

Lipophilic hormones: steroids,
thyroid hormones, calcitriol

G protein-coupled receptors
→ adenylate cyclase (cAMP),
phospholipase C (IP₃, Ca²⁺, DAG)

Tyrosine kinase receptors
(insulin, growth factors)
→ IRS, PI3K/Akt, Ras-MAPK

Nuclear (intracellular) receptors
→ hormone response element
in DNA (HRE)

Slow response (hours–days):
gene transcription,
new protein synthesis

Iodide (I⁻) from blood → NIS (Na⁺/I⁻ symporter)
on the basal membrane (enhanced by TSH)

Pendrin → colloid; thyroid peroxidase (H₂O₂):
I⁻ → I⁰ (oxidation)

Iodination of thyroglobulin tyrosines:
MIT, DIT (organification)

Coupling (thyroid peroxidase):
DIT + DIT → T₄;  MIT + DIT → T₃

Colloid endocytosis → thyroglobulin proteolysis
in lysosomes → T₄, T₃ into blood (TSH)

Peripheral deiodinase (Se): T₄ → T₃ (active)
or rT₃ (inactive)

Calcitonin (C cells):
inhibits osteoclasts when Ca²⁺ ↑

Bone: osteoclast activation
(RANKL) → Ca²⁺ and phosphate released

Glomerulus: ultrafiltration ≈ 180 l/day
(protein-free plasma; GFR ≈ 90–120 ml/min)

Loop of Henle: NKCC2 (Na⁺, K⁺, 2Cl⁻);
countercurrent — medullary hyperosmolality

Collecting duct: ENaC, K⁺ and H⁺ secretion
(aldosterone); water — aquaporin-2 (vasopressin)

Tubular cell: CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃
(carbonic anhydrase) → H⁺ + HCO₃⁻

Astrocyte: glutamate is taken up
(EAAT) → glutamine
(glutamine synthetase, ATP, NH₃)

Glycolysis in astrocyte → lactate →
to neuron (energy, “lactate shuttle”)

GABAergic neuron: glutamate →
GABA (glutamate decarboxylase, B₆)
Action potential reaches the presynaptic terminal

Botulinum toxin cleaves SNARE
→ no transmitter release

Vesicle exocytosis (SNARE proteins:
synaptobrevin, syntaxin, SNAP-25) → transmitter release

Ionotropic receptors
(nAChR, NMDA/AMPA, GABA-A):
fast response (ms)

Metabotropic receptors
(G protein: mAChR, adrenergic,
dopamine, GABA-B): slow

Termination: enzymatic breakdown
(acetylcholinesterase, MAO, COMT) or
reuptake (transporters — SSRI target)
